title: Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome): clenched hands + micrognathia + VSD
vignette: A newborn is examined immediately after an induced vaginal delivery for fetal growth retardation. On visual inspection, the infant has low-set ears, a small mandible, and a prominent occiput. The neonate has a weak cry and increased tone of the extremities, including clenched hands with second and fifth digits on top of the third and fourth digits. Cardiac auscultation reveals a harsh, IV/VI holosystolic murmur heard best at the left sternal border. The infant is transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit for further workup and management. Which of the following is the most likely chromosomal abnormality in this infant?

clues.note: Intrauterine growth restriction is characteristic of trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome).

clues.text: low-set ears, a small mandible, and a prominent occiput
clues.note: Micrognathia (small jaw), low-set ears, and a prominent occiput are classic dysmorphic features of Edwards syndrome.

clues.text: clenched hands with second and fifth digits on top of the third and fourth digits
clues.note: Clenched hands with OVERLAPPING fingers are a hallmark of trisomy 18.

clues.text: harsh, IV/VI holosystolic murmur heard best at the left sternal border
clues.note: A holosystolic murmur at the left sternal border suggests a ventricular septal defect, a common congenital heart defect in Edwards syndrome.

whatMatters: Growth restriction + micrognathia + low-set ears + prominent occiput + clenched hands with OVERLAPPING fingers + a VSD = trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), 47,XX,+18. Answer D. It results from meiotic nondisjunction (risk rises with maternal age); most affected infants die within the first year.
strategy: Match the dysmorphology to the trisomy. Edwards (18): growth restriction, micrognathia, prominent occiput, clenched hands with overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom feet, VSD. Reject Patau (13): midline defects, holoprosencephaly, cleft lip/palate, POLYDACTYLY. Down (21): flat facies, single palmar crease, hypotonia. Cri-du-chat (5p-): high-pitched cry, microcephaly. DiGeorge (22q11): cardiac outflow defects, hypocalcemia, thymic aplasia.

eliminations.label: 5p deletion - cri-du-chat
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cri-du-chat syndrome (5p deletion): high-pitched 'cat-like' cry, microcephaly, hypotonia, intellectual disability. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this infant has overlapping fingers, micrognathia, and hypertonia - Edwards features, not cri-du-chat. ✅ Correct if: a mewing high-pitched cry with microcephaly.

eliminations.label: 22q11 deletion - DiGeorge
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: DiGeorge syndrome: conotruncal cardiac anomalies, thymic hypoplasia, hypocalcemia, cleft palate. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the overlapping-fingers/rocker-bottom-feet/growth-restriction picture is Edwards, not the DiGeorge phenotype. ✅ Correct if: cardiac outflow defect + hypocalcemia + recurrent infections.

eliminations.label: 47,XX,+13 - Patau syndrome
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: trisomy 13 (Patau): midline defects, holoprosencephaly, cleft lip/palate, POLYDACTYLY, omphalocele. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this infant has overlapping fingers (not polydactyly) and lacks midline/holoprosencephaly features - favoring trisomy 18. ✅ Correct if: cleft lip/palate + polydactyly + holoprosencephaly.

eliminations.label: 47,XX,+21 - Down syndrome
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: trisomy 21 (Down): flat facial profile, upslanting palpebral fissures, single transverse palmar crease, HYPOtonia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this infant has HYPERtonia and clenched overlapping fingers - Edwards, not Down. ✅ Correct if: flat facies + single palmar crease + hypotonia.

reasoning: Growth restriction + micrognathia + prominent occiput + clenched overlapping fingers + VSD
This constellation is classic for trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome)
mechanism: Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome) is a complete extra copy of chromosome 18, usually from meiotic NONDISJUNCTION during oogenesis (risk increases with advanced maternal age). Characteristic features include intrauterine growth restriction; craniofacial dysmorphism (micrognathia, low-set ears, prominent occiput); marked HYPERTONIA with CLENCHED HANDS and OVERLAPPING fingers (index over middle, fifth over fourth); ROCKER-BOTTOM feet; and congenital anomalies of the heart (e.g., ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus), kidneys (horseshoe kidney), and GI tract (omphalocele, Meckel diverticulum). Prenatal ultrasound often shows growth restriction. It is the second most common autosomal trisomy after Down syndrome; prognosis is poor - most affected infants die in utero or within the first year (about half of liveborns die by ~2 weeks). Mnemonic 'Election age 18' (Edwards). The distractors are other syndromes: Patau (trisomy 13, midline/polydactyly), Down (21, hypotonia/single crease), cri-du-chat (5p-, high-pitched cry), and DiGeorge (22q11, cardiac outflow + hypocalcemia).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Genetics > trisomy 18 (Edwards): growth restriction, micrognathia, prominent occiput, clenched hands with overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom feet, VSD; nondisjunction; poor prognosis. Contrast trisomy 13/21, cri-du-chat, DiGeorge.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Overlapping fingers + micrognathia + hypertonia + VSD pin trisomy 18 over the other syndromes.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on micrognathia, rocker-bottom feet, nondisjunction, holoprosencephaly, or trisomy karyotype notation? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Patau (13) = polydactyly/cleft/holoprosencephaly; Down (21) = hypotonia/single crease; cri-du-chat = high-pitched cry; DiGeorge = 22q11.
